ANIMAL KINGDOM IN THE TREE OF LIFE
=====================================

EUKARYOTA
|
+-- PLANTAE (photosynthetic; cell walls)
+-- FUNGI (absorptive; cell walls; chitin)
+-- PROTISTA (paraphyletic; diverse)
+-- ANIMALIA (~1.5 million described spp)
    |
    +-- PARAZOA (no true tissues)
    |   +-- Porifera (sponges: ~10,000 spp)
    |   +-- Placozoa (~3 spp; simplest animals)
    |
    +-- EUMETAZOA (true tissues)
        |
        +-- RADIATA (radial symmetry)
        |   +-- Cnidaria (jellyfish, corals: ~10,000 spp)
        |   +-- Ctenophora (comb jellies: ~100 spp)
        |
        +-- BILATERIA (bilateral symmetry; ~99% of animals)
            |
            +-- PROTOSTOMIA
            |   +-- Lophotrochozoa
            |   |   +-- Mollusca (~100,000 spp)
            |   |   +-- Annelida (~22,000 spp)
            |   |   +-- Platyhelminthes (~20,000 spp)
            |   |   +-- Brachiopoda, Bryozoa, Phoronida
            |   |
            |   +-- Ecdysozoa
            |       +-- Arthropoda (~1,000,000 spp) <- LARGEST PHYLUM
            |       +-- Nematoda (~25,000 spp described; ~1M estimated)
            |       +-- Tardigrada, Priapulida, others
            |
            +-- DEUTEROSTOMIA
                +-- Echinodermata (~7,000 spp)
                +-- Hemichordata (~120 spp)
                +-- CHORDATA (~65,000 spp)
                    +-- Urochordata (tunicates)
                    +-- Cephalochordata (lancelets)
                    +-- VERTEBRATA (~58,000 spp)

ANIMAL DIAGNOSTIC CHARACTER SUITE
===================================

REQUIRED:
  1. Eukaryotic (membrane-bound nuclei)
  2. Multicellular (no single-celled animals)
  3. Heterotrophic (cannot fix own carbon; must ingest)
  4. No cell walls (vs plants + fungi)
  5. Most: motile at some life stage
  6. Most: sexual reproduction (haploid gametes fusing -> diploid)
  7. Most: embryonic development through blastula stage

DERIVED CHARACTERS (not universal):
  Nervous system (absent in Porifera, Placozoa)
  Muscles (absent in Porifera)
  Bilateral symmetry (absent in Porifera, Cnidaria, many Echinodermata)
  Coelom (absent or modified in many)
  Segmentation (present in Annelida, Arthropoda, Chordata; convergent)

ZOOLOGY SUBDISCIPLINES
========================
+-------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Comparative morph | Body plans, symmetry, organ homology     |
| Physiology        | Organ systems, homeostasis               |
| Developmental bio | Embryology, evo-devo, Hox genes          |
| Ethology          | Behavior: mechanisms + function          |
| Behavioral ecol.  | Foraging, mating, altruism               |
| Ecology           | Populations, communities, ecosystems     |
| Systematics       | Taxonomy, phylogenetics                  |
| Evolutionary bio  | Speciation, adaptation, macroevolution   |
| Parasitology      | Host-parasite interactions               |
| Conservation      | Species + habitat protection             |
+-------------------+------------------------------------------+

PROTOSTOME vs DEUTEROSTOME
=============================

PROTOSTOME ("mouth first"):
  Blastopore -> mouth
  Spiral, determinate cleavage
  Schizocoelomate (coelom from solid mesoderm splitting)
  Groups: Arthropoda, Mollusca, Annelida, Nematoda, Platyhelminthes

DEUTEROSTOME ("mouth second"):
  Blastopore -> anus; mouth forms secondarily
  Radial, indeterminate cleavage
  Enterocoelous (coelom from gut outpocketings)
  Groups: Echinodermata, Chordata

DEVELOPMENTAL FATE:
  Protostome determinate cleavage:
    Each blastomere fate fixed early
    Remove one cell -> defect (mosaic development)
  Deuterostome indeterminate cleavage:
    Fate not fixed at first divisions
    Separate identical twins are possible
    Remove one cell at 2-cell stage -> two complete embryos
    (basis for natural twinning in mammals)
